To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the HLA-DR region has undergone an extensive reorganization in the primate lineage and (ii) the evolutionary history of DRB genes is complex, with a combination of gene duplication, gene deletion, and gene recombination events.

(i) at least four ancestral DR genes have been present in the genome of the common ancestor of Old World monkeys and hominoids; (ii) two of these ancestral DR genes have survived in the genomes of all primates studied and are locked in the genomes as pseudogenes; and (iii) the remaining two ancestral genes have evolved into DRB5 genes in Old World monkeys and into DRB1 genes in hominoids.

(1) the HLA-DR locus is a mosaic of several ancestral DRB gene lineages, which have evolved in different ways, and (2) the evolutionary relationships between these lineages are complex and difficult to trace.
